review.causal_identification_verdict: The causal identification strategy is sound in design but unexecuted. The cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment (F2) is the correct decisive intervention: it isolates the effect of the learning projection g(T_K) by holding the acting winner, initial skill state, updater, verifier, and update seed fixed. However, the historical R3 runner cannot implement this (it uses independent K=1 shadows and forbids nonselected failures from updater input), and no scientific experiment has been run. The causal chain (winner selection -> censoring of failure evidence -> weaker persistent skill -> lower future frozen performance) requires independent verification of each link; the identity alone does not establish the chain.
review.experiment_sufficiency_verdict: The experiments are entirely insufficient. No scientific experiment has been run. The decisive F2 cloned-state projection-null experiment has not been executed, and the existing R3 runner is explicitly non-executable for the R4 same-pool intervention. The paper cannot be evaluated for ICLR without at minimum the F2 experiment demonstrating that changing the learning projection on identical pools changes future frozen skill. The proposed F1 (controlled procedure suite), F3 (prospective prediction), F4 (longitudinal evolution), F5 (topology interaction), and F6 (second substrate) are all downstream of F2 and cannot rescue the paper if F2 fails.

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Execute the F2 cloned-state experiment: fix one pre-update skill state S, one task batch, one exact K-pool T_K with frozen hashes, one acting winner, and one updater; clone S into arms differing only in g(T_K) (winner-only vs. precommitted rejected witness vs. contrast packet); freeze all skills and evaluate on a common held-out K=1 probe. If changing g(T_K) produces no directional difference in future frozen skill, stop.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: The central causal mechanism is entirely untested: no cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment (F2) has been executed, and the existing R3 runner cannot implement it (it uses independent K=1 shadows, not same-pool precommitted rollouts, and forbids nonselected failures from updater input).

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Demote CADP to an optional ablation and replace the primary method with the minimal Rejected-Witness projection (feeding a precommitted nonserved failure witness from the same pool to the updater). Add SkillCAT as a mandatory baseline; if SkillCAT-style contrast explains the full effect without the serving-selection causal chain, reduce to an application or stop.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: CADP is a direct method collision with SkillCAT (arXiv:2606.13317), which already combines same-task success/failure pairing, first-divergence extraction, contrastive skill editing, and replay validation in a persistent external-skill pipeline.

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Delete all theoretical claims except the independence-free rescue-censoring identity A_K - A_1 = Pr(Y_1=0, max_i Y_i=1) = Gamma_K(Q), explicitly labeled as a definitional tool, not a theorem. Remove the MI bound, the i.i.d. curve as an empirical law, and the layer-cake identity as an extension.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: The theoretical contributions are non-substantive: the mutual-information bound I(Z; g_win(T_K)) <= I(Z; T_K) is a vacuous data-processing inequality for a fixed LLM updater; the Gamma-times-delta factorization is a tautological decomposition whose content is entirely empirical; the i.i.d. Bernoulli peak p*(K) is an elementary order-statistic calculation; and the continuous-verifier layer-cake identity is a standard representation.

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Delete all claims that failure feedback is useful or that outcome filtering discards branch structure. Reframe the paper strictly as a mechanism-level study of serving-induced selective trajectory logging, citing these works as established prior art.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: The claim that failure feedback is useful for skill evolution and that outcome-based filtering discards useful branch structure is already reduced by prior work (Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills, arXiv:2608.02636; TopoCurate, arXiv:2603.01714).

issues_not_worth_chasing: The i.i.d. Bernoulli intermediate-difficulty peak p*(K) as an empirical law (correlated rollouts destroy the peak location; it is only a reference curve).
The continuous-verifier layer-cake identity as a substantive extension (adds no empirical content beyond the binary case unless a threshold policy is actually used).
The information-theoretic statement I(Z; g_win(T_K)) <= I(Z; T_K) as a scientific contribution (vacuous for a fixed LLM updater).
The Gamma-times-delta factorization as a theoretical result (tautological; scientific content is entirely in whether delta_z is positive and predictable).
Any claim that bounded validation-gated skill editing or rejected-edit memory is novel (already established by SkillOpt and SkillHEX).
review.novelty_after_skillcat_topocurate: The only potentially novel contribution is the mechanism-level causal claim that serving-time winner selection endogenously censors diagnostic failures from an external persistent updater, testable through a same-pool projection intervention. However, this is currently buried under method components (CADP) that are direct collisions with SkillCAT (success/failure pairing, first-divergence extraction, contrastive editing, replay validation) and broader claims about failure utility and outcome filtering already established by Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills and TopoCurate. The Rejected-Witness projection is the minimal method that follows from the mechanism, but it is not novel as a skill-editing technique.
repairs_that_could_change_verdict: Run the cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment (F2) and demonstrate a statistically significant directional effect of changing g(T_K) on future frozen skill J(U(S,g(T_K))) in the preregistered direction, particularly in mixed rescue pools with positive estimated delta.

Demonstrate that the Rejected-Witness projection (not CADP) suffices to rescue the effect, and that a source-faithful SkillCAT-style contrast baseline does not reproduce the full effect without the serving-selection causal chain.
Show that the prospective Gamma-times-delta law predicts held-out family sign and rank ordering on unseen task cells, validating the mechanism beyond post-hoc explanation.
review.single_sentence_verdict: R17 proposes a potentially real but narrow mechanism-level claim—that serving-time winner selection censors diagnostic failures from a persistent updater—but it is currently a design document with zero experimental evidence, a method (CADP) that directly collides with SkillCAT, theoretical contributions that are vacuous or tautological, and a decisive causal experiment (F2) that has not been run and cannot be run with the existing runner.
review.strongest_reject_reason: The paper proposes a mechanism-level causal claim—that winner-only serving selection censors diagnostic failures from a persistent updater, degrading future skill—but provides zero experimental evidence for this phenomenon. The decisive cloned-state projection-null experiment (F2) has not been run, and the historical R3 runner is explicitly non-executable for the R4 same-pool intervention. Meanwhile, the proposed method (CADP) is a direct collision with SkillCAT (success/failure pairing, first-divergence extraction, contrastive skill editing, replay validation), and the broader claims about failure utility and outcome-filtering discarding branch structure are already established by Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills and TopoCurate. The theoretical contributions are either vacuous (data-processing inequality for a fixed LLM updater), tautological (Gamma-times-delta factorization), or elementary (i.i.d. Bernoulli order statistics). Without the F2 experiment demonstrating that changing the learning projection g(T_K) on identical pools changes future frozen skill, the paper is an unphenomenological design document with method components already published elsewhere.
review.theory_depth_verdict: The theoretical contributions are shallow or vacuous. The rescue-censoring identity A_K - A_1 = Gamma_K(Q) is a definitional tool, not a theorem. The i.i.d. Bernoulli peak p*(K) is an elementary order-statistic calculation. The mutual-information bound is a vacuous data-processing inequality for a fixed LLM updater. The Gamma-times-delta factorization is a tautological decomposition whose scientific content is entirely in whether delta_z is positive and predictable (an empirical claim). The continuous-verifier layer-cake identity is a standard representation. The theory does not provide deep insight beyond the definitional identity.
